checks.label: Photo Picker Enforcement (Android 13+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'com\.google\.android\.providers\.media\.module|com\.android\.providers\.media' | head -1; fi
checks.description: Android 13 (API 33) introduced the system Photo Picker so apps can pick images/video without the full READ_MEDIA_IMAGES permission. The picker is delivered by the MediaProvider module; its presence is required for apps to use the privacy-preserving picker API. On A13+ this check confirms the provider exists. On pre-A13 builds it reports PRE_A13_SDK_<n> as informational.
checks.remediation: On Android 13+, ensure com.google.android.providers.media.module (Mainline) or com.android.providers.media is present and updated via Play system updates. Encourage in-house apps to use ACTION_PICK_IMAGES instead of requesting READ_MEDIA_*.

checks.label: Granular Media Permissions Granted (READ_MEDIA_*)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | sed 's/package://' | while read pkg; do D=$(dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep 'granted=true'); for P in android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES android.permission.READ_MEDIA_VIDEO android.permission.READ_MEDIA_AUDIO; do if printf '%s\n' "$D" | grep -q "$P"; then echo "$pkg $P"; fi; done; done | head -20; fi
checks.description: On Android 13+ the legacy READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission was split into READ_MEDIA_IMAGES, READ_MEDIA_VIDEO and READ_MEDIA_AUDIO. Enumerates every third-party app that has been granted any of these granular media permissions. On a kiosk, POS or medical device the result should usually be empty - the audit lets the operator confirm only intentional apps see the user media library.
checks.remediation: Revoke READ_MEDIA_IMAGES/VIDEO/AUDIO from apps that do not need direct gallery access: 'pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES'. Encourage apps to use the system Photo Picker instead.

checks.label: POST_NOTIFICATIONS Runtime Permission Audit
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | sed 's/package://' | while read pkg; do if dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -E "granted=true" | grep -q 'android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS'; then echo "$pkg"; fi; done | head -20; fi
checks.description: Android 13 turned POST_NOTIFICATIONS into a runtime permission. Lists every third-party app that currently holds it. Useful as an inventory check on locked-down deployments (kiosk, POS, medical) where the operator wants to confirm only approved apps can raise notifications, since notification listeners and the Identity Check flow both interact with this surface.
checks.remediation: Revoke POST_NOTIFICATIONS from apps that should not raise notifications: 'pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS'. Review remaining grants against the approved app list.

checks.label: Foreground Service Type Declared (Android 14+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 34 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A14_SDK_$SDK"; else dumpsys activity services 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'ServiceRecord|foregroundServiceType' | grep -B1 'foregroundServiceType=0\b' | grep ServiceRecord | head -10; fi
checks.description: Android 14 (API 34) requires every foreground service to declare a foregroundServiceType (camera, microphone, location, dataSync, mediaPlayback, etc). A running FGS with type 0 on an A14+ build indicates either a legacy app targeting an old SDK that has been allowed to skip the requirement, or a service that worked around the new declaration rule. Either case is worth investigating because untyped FGS bypass the per-type runtime-permission gating Android 14 enforces.
checks.remediation: Identify the offending app (ServiceRecord shows package/class) and update it to target SDK 34+ and declare the correct foregroundServiceType in its manifest. Remove apps that cannot be updated and rely on untyped foreground services.

checks.label: Theft Detection Lock Enabled (Android 15)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 35 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A15_SDK_$SDK"; else V=$(settings get secure theft_detection_lock_enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && echo UNSET || echo "$V"; fi
checks.description: Android 15 ships Theft Detection Lock: the device uses on-device ML on accelerometer and connectivity signals to detect a snatch (sudden motion plus immediate disconnect from known networks) and auto-locks. On consumer phones used by field staff this is a meaningful loss-of-control mitigation. 1 = enabled (SAFE). UNSET = the user has not opted in OR this build does not expose the setting via the 'secure' namespace - reported as INFO, not a finding, because the exact key has not been confirmed across OEM A15 builds. Verify on real hardware before treating UNSET as a gap.
checks.remediation: Enable in Settings > Security and privacy > Device unlock > Theft protection > Theft Detection Lock, or push via DPC. For fleet deployments, enable this together with Offline Device Lock and Remote Lock.

checks.label: Identity Check Enabled (Android 15)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 35 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A15_SDK_$SDK"; else V=$(settings get secure identity_check_enabled 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && echo UNSET || echo "$V"; fi
checks.description: Android 15 Identity Check requires biometric authentication for sensitive settings changes (lockscreen credential changes, factory reset, password manager access, disabling Find My Device) when the device is outside a trusted location. Defeats the 'thief watches you type the PIN, then locks you out' attack pattern. 1 = enabled (SAFE). UNSET = user has not opted in OR this build does not expose the setting via the 'secure' namespace - reported as INFO, not a finding, because the exact key has not been confirmed across OEM A15 builds. Verify on real hardware.
checks.remediation: Enable in Settings > Security and privacy > Device unlock > Identity Check. Requires Class 3 (Strong) biometric. Combine with Theft Detection Lock for full A15 anti-theft posture.

checks.label: Restricted Networking Mode Active
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 33 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A13_SDK_$SDK"; else dumpsys netpolicy 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'restrictBackground|restrictedMode|mRestricted' | head -5; fi
checks.description: Reports the current state of Android's restricted networking / data saver policy from netpolicy. Restricted networking mode caps background data for non-allowlisted apps and is a useful indicator on locked-down POS, kiosk and field devices where only the operator app should reach the network. Pre-A13 builds are skipped.
checks.remediation: Enable Data Saver / Restricted Networking in Settings > Network and internet > Data Saver and add only the operator app to the unrestricted allowlist. For DPC-managed devices, push the policy via DevicePolicyManager.setNetworkLoggingEnabled() and per-app background data rules.

checks.label: Advanced Protection Mode (Android 16+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 36 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A16_SDK_$SDK"; else V=$(settings get global advanced_protection_mode 2>/dev/null); [ -z "$V" ] || [ "$V" = "null" ] && echo UNSET || echo "$V"; fi
checks.description: Device-level Advanced Protection Mode shipped in Android 16 (API 36), the on-device counterpart to Google account Advanced Protection. When enabled it forces stricter defaults: MTE on supported chips, blocks 2G fallback, blocks USB data on lock, disables sideloading, hardens WebView SafeBrowsing. Recommended for journalists, executives, security staff and high-value POS/kiosk fleets. 1 = enabled (SAFE). UNSET = not opted in OR the setting is not exposed via the 'global' namespace on this build - reported as INFO because the key has not been confirmed across OEM A16 builds.
checks.remediation: Enable in Settings > Security and privacy > Advanced Protection. Note this disables sideloading and some debugging features. For account-level Advanced Protection enrollment, see g.co/advancedprotection.

checks.label: Local Network Access Permission Grants (Android 17+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 37 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A17_SDK_$SDK"; else pm list packages -3 2>/dev/null | sed 's/package://' | while read pkg; do if dumpsys package "$pkg" 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'granted=true' | grep -q 'android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK'; then echo "$pkg"; fi; done | head -20; fi
checks.description: Android 17 (API 37) introduced the ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK runtime permission (NEARBY_DEVICES group). Apps must hold it to reach the local network - LAN device discovery and direct socket connections to other hosts on the same network. This enumerates every third-party app granted it. On a POS, kiosk, medical or IoT deployment only the operator/integration app should reach the LAN; unexpected grants widen the local attack surface and can enable lateral movement or data exfiltration to other devices on the network. Empty output on A17+ means no third-party app holds it (SAFE). Pre-A17 builds report PRE_A17_SDK_<n>.
checks.remediation: Revoke from apps that do not need LAN access: 'pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.ACCESS_LOCAL_NETWORK'. Prefer the system-mediated device pickers where possible, and review remaining grants against the approved app list.

checks.label: Private Space Profile Present (Android 15+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 35 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A15_SDK_$SDK"; else P=$(pm list users -v 2>/dev/null | grep -i private | head -3); [ -z "$P" ] && echo NO_PRIVATE_SPACE || echo "$P"; fi
checks.description: Android 15 (API 35) added Private Space: a separate, biometric/PIN-locked user profile (user type profile.PRIVATE) whose apps and notifications are hidden from the main profile and paused when locked. On a personal or BYOD device its presence is a privacy-hardening plus (sensitive apps isolated from casual device access). On a locked-down single-purpose deployment (POS, kiosk, medical) an unexpected private profile is a review item because it provides a hidden app installation surface. Reported as INFO either way: NO_PRIVATE_SPACE means no private profile exists; a line naming a private profile means one is configured. Pre-A15 builds report PRE_A15_SDK_<n>.
checks.remediation: Nothing to fix by default. On single-purpose fleets, review any private profile found and remove it if not sanctioned: identify the user id from 'pm list users -v' and run 'pm remove-user <id>'. On personal devices used by high-risk staff, consider recommending Private Space for sensitive apps.

checks.label: Intrusion Logging / Advanced Protection Service State (Android 16+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 36 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A16_SDK_$SDK"; else D=$(dumpsys advanced_protection 2>/dev/null | head -20); [ -z "$D" ] && echo NO_SERVICE_OUTPUT || echo "$D"; fi
checks.description: Android 16's Advanced Protection includes Intrusion Logging (rolling out since the Android 16 December 2025 update): activity logs (USB connections, network info, app installs, Bluetooth pairing, lock screen events) are backed up end-to-end encrypted to the user's Google account in a tamper-resistant way, so a suspected compromise can be investigated after the fact. State lives in the system advanced_protection service; this check dumps its state for manual review because the dump format is undocumented and varies by build. NO_SERVICE_OUTPUT means the service is absent or empty on this build (common on non-Pixel A16 builds until the feature reaches them). Pre-A16 builds report PRE_A16_SDK_<n>.
checks.remediation: For high-risk users, enable Advanced Protection (Settings > Security and privacy > Advanced Protection) and opt in to Intrusion Logging when prompted, choosing a Google account for the encrypted log backup. Review the dumped state to confirm the expected subfeatures are on.

checks.label: Advanced Protection Subfeature Audit (Android 17+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 37 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A17_SDK_$SDK"; else D=$(dumpsys advanced_protection 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'enabled|feature|usb|accessibility|webgpu|unlock|scam|mte' | head -15); [ -z "$D" ] && echo NO_SERVICE_OUTPUT || echo "$D"; fi
checks.description: Android 17 expands Advanced Protection beyond the Android 16 baseline: it removes accessibility-service access from non-accessibility apps, disables device-to-device unlocking, disables Chrome WebGPU, and integrates scam detection for chat notifications, alongside the existing USB lock protection and MTE enforcement. The companion MOD-A16-APP-001 check only confirms the mode master toggle; this check extracts the per-subfeature lines from the advanced_protection service dump for manual review, since subfeature availability differs by OEM and rollout wave. NO_SERVICE_OUTPUT means the service dump exposes nothing greppable on this build. Pre-A17 builds report PRE_A17_SDK_<n>.
checks.remediation: Enable Advanced Protection in Settings > Security and privacy > Advanced Protection and review the dumped subfeature state against the deployment's threat model. For managed fleets, Android Enterprise support for Advanced Protection is rolling out during 2026; track DPC support to enforce it by policy.

checks.label: KeyMint Version / Post-Quantum Readiness (Android 17+)
checks.command: SDK=$(getprop ro.build.version.sdk 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$SDK" ] || [ "$SDK" -lt 37 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "PRE_A17_SDK_$SDK"; else F=$(pm list features 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'hardware_keystore' | head -2); K=$(getprop ro.hardware.keystore 2>/dev/null); echo "${F:-NO_KEYSTORE_FEATURE} hal=${K:-unknown}"; fi
checks.description: Android 17 introduces post-quantum cryptography support: devices with a new-enough KeyMint can generate ML-DSA (Module-Lattice Digital Signature Algorithm) keys in secure hardware, and the platform adds APK Signature Scheme v3.2 combining classical and ML-DSA signatures. This reports the android.hardware.hardware_keystore feature version (the number after '=' is the KeyMint feature level, e.g. 300) plus the keystore HAL property, so an auditor can record whether the device's secure hardware generation is PQC-capable. Informational: PQC availability depends on the KeyMint version shipped by the SoC vendor, and most 2026 fleet hardware will not have it yet. Pre-A17 builds report PRE_A17_SDK_<n>.
checks.remediation: Nothing to fix on-device. For long-lived deployments handling data that must stay confidential for many years, prefer hardware whose KeyMint version supports ML-DSA key generation when refreshing the fleet.
